Source:[Nebius Group Third Quarter 2026 Letter to Shareholders](https://assets.nebius.com/assets/5bc733ff-bed7-415c-af10-74ce7881a764/Nebius-SHL-2026-Q3.pdf?cache-buster=2026-11-12T11:54:28.601Z&_gl=1*cbxacv*_gcl_au*MTAxMjAxMDgyLjE3OTQ0ODU1Nzc.)

## Key Metrics Overview

* Excluding contracts with terms of one year or less: the proportion of capital expenditures covered by advance payments exceeds 100% (compared to 50–60% in the second quarter).
* Comparable contract return period: 1 year and 7 months (Q2: 1 year and 10 months)
* ![](https://record.futunn.com/news-editor-imgs/20261112/public/17944889513103181507138.png?imageMogr2/quality/minsize/1/ignore-error/1/format/webp)Goal: Achieve pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027
* New business volume: Total contract value (TCV) signed since the beginning of the third quarter: USD 12 billion
* Annual Contract Value (ACV) per MW: >$25 million (Q2: $20–25 million)
* Q3 Group Revenue: $981 million, up 571% year over year; Nebius AI Cloud Adjusted EBITDA Margin 53%
* Preliminary guidance for 2027: Revenue of $12.0–$13.0 billion; capital expenditures of $40.0–$45.0 billion, 75–85% of which will be covered by customer prepayments and investment-grade asset-backed financing.
* 2027 customer expected prepayments: $17–20 billion; 2026 committed prepayments already secured: $10 billion

> Notes: (1) Capital expenditure coverage statistics include contracts of one year or longer, encompassing GPU, data center construction, and leasehold improvement costs. (2) ACV: Annual Contract Value. (3) Weighted average is calculated based on contracts with terms of up to five years.

## CEO Open Letter

Arkady Volozh, Founder and CEO

Dear Shareholders:

The third quarter of 2026 once again confirmed the strong performance of the business we are building. Market demand remains exceptionally robust, and we have put in place comprehensive mechanisms to capitalize on growth opportunities.

Unlike typical cloud providers, we do not merely build and operate data centers and computing resources; nor are we like inference service providers that simply offer cloud services on top of leased compute.

Nebius strikes a balance between the two: we independently design, build, and operate our underlying infrastructure, develop cloud-platform software, and deliver managed AI services that run on it. This is a hyperscale cloud‑provider model; as an integrated system, it supports all compute‑intensive AI workloads, covering the entire end‑to‑end pipeline—from model training and post‑training to inference, agent search, and execution. This enables us to fully capitalize on the current industry growth opportunities.

Turning to our third-quarter results, we secured the most favorable commercial contract to date this quarter:

1. Customers are signing contracts with longer durations, higher unit prices, and a greater proportion of upfront payments. In Q3, the upfront payments on signed contracts already exceeded the total capital expenditures (including data center construction and network investments), whereas in Q2 this ratio was only 50–60%. To date, this upward trend has continued into Q4 for newly signed contracts.
2. Driven by higher contracted prices under new agreements, the average investment payback period for comparable 1‑ to 3‑year contracts improved from 1 year and 10 months in the second quarter to 1 year and 7 months; this return covers both operating costs and capital expenditures¹.
3. Our hosted inference platform, Token Factory, is on track to generate annualized revenue in the hundreds of millions of dollars; Q3 contract value surged 17-fold quarter-over-quarter, and this is just the early stage of our business.
4. The customer base continues to expand: Native AI companies are steadily increasing the scale of their collaborations, and we have completed initial signings with several leading enterprise data and AI platforms. Our partnership models include direct customer engagements as well as joint sales initiatives with channel partners.
5. Through innovative pricing mechanisms such as reserve auctions and real-time spot computing power pricing, the true value of computing power is determined by the market. This approach not only provides customers with more ways to access the Nebius platform but also enables us to gain real-time insights into actual market demand.

The foundation of our business model lies in computing power supply, supported by a flexible and diversified global footprint of data centers, partners, and local access to electricity resources:

* We prioritize building our own data centers to better control project implementation and achieve superior economic returns. All self-built sites have been delivered on schedule or even ahead of time, and in the future, the vast majority of new gigawatt-scale computing capacity will come from our proprietary facilities.
* Third-party co-hosted data centers have experienced delivery delays; for example, at the New Jersey site, we are switching the power supply to Bloom Energy's sustainable fuel cells. The first batch of generator sets has been installed, and we are currently expanding computing capacity.

> ¹ Based on comparable 1–3 year contracts, server equipment is depreciated over a 5-year period.

In recent weeks, the industry has been closely watching the funding sources for the expansion of AI infrastructure.

We remain focused on building a long-term, healthy, and profitable business. We will continue to invest in computing infrastructure, platform product development, and our go-to-market team.

Our self-developed, self-built model helps us secure more favorable contract pricing and commercial terms while reducing infrastructure costs, ultimately driving higher profit margins. This approach has already begun to deliver results, and we are pursuing prudent financing backed by customer prepayments and a strong balance sheet:

* We expect that 75%–85% of our capital expenditures in 2027 will be financed through customer prepayments and asset‑backed financing secured by contracts signed with investment‑grade customers; we also have a wide range of alternative financing channels available.
* The company has low debt costs, a healthy balance sheet, and holds cash along with several strategic equity investments.
* When external financing costs are favorable, we will opportunistically pursue additional external financing.

Updated Fiscal 2026 Earnings Guidance

Affected by the deferral of some revenue for this year to early 2027:

* For the full year 2026, revenue is expected to be at the lower end of the original guidance range of $3.0–$3.4 billion; adjusted EBITDA margin is approximately 40%.
* The annualized recurring revenue (ARR), originally expected to be achieved in December, is now projected for February 2027—earlier than the New Jersey site's full‑capacity commissioning.

Preliminary Business Outlook for 2027

* Leveraging the aforementioned structural advantages, we expect to achieve breakeven on a pre-tax basis by the end of 2027.
* Revenue target: USD 12–13 billion; this projection is based on conservative assumptions regarding the ramp-up of computing capacity. We continue to plan for the addition of more than 1 GW of new computing capacity each year.
* Capital expenditures of $40–45 billion, with a prudent and diversified capital allocation strategy.
* As our business matures, we are transitioning to performance metrics that more accurately reflect our underlying operating performance: beginning in 2027, we will disclose guidance for revenue and profit before tax.

Our confidence in the fundamentals of our business remains unwavering, and the market opportunities ahead remain vast. We will continue to move forward.

## Customer: Deeper engagement, broader customer base

Market demand is undeniable. Since the start of Q3, customers have secured over $12 billion in contract value for Nebius under historically favorable terms, and we still have substantial mining capacity available for sale.

We independently determine our computing power sales approach and commercial terms. This quarter, we simultaneously opened additional procurement channels for customers; even with more options available, they continue to accept the contract conditions we set: larger contract sizes, longer durations, higher unit prices, and greater upfront payments. The Q3 contracting activity, as well as the situation in Q4 to date, fully confirms this trend.

### Prepayments: Customer prepayments now cover or even exceed capital expenditures.

1. In Q3, the proportion of capital expenditures covered by advance payments on signed contracts exceeded 100%, compared with only 50–60% in Q2; this trend continued into Q4.
2. In Q3, more than 90% of the total contract value signed included advance payment terms; the weighted-average proportion of advance payments to contract value increased by approximately 20 percentage points quarter over quarter.
3. Renewals of existing computing power also generate upfront payments, boosting the return on existing assets. Capital expenditures for existing computing capacity have already been recovered, and the additional upfront payments can fund the next phase of infrastructure development.

## Return Cycle: Accelerated Returns, Enhanced Operational Visibility

1. Compared with the 1‑ to 3‑year contract return period, which shortened from 1 year and 10 months in Q2 to 1 year and 7 months in Q3, the primary driver was an increase in new contract signing prices. The returns cover both operating costs and capital expenditures, and the calculations do not include gains from upfront payments.
2. Nebius AI Cloud has secured five-year customer contracts, with an annual contract value per megawatt exceeding previous quarterly levels. These long-term agreements combine duration, scale, and upfront payments: customers lock in computing power at current prices for the long term.
3. The new five-year AI cloud contract optimizes the customer contract term structure, delivering predictable high-margin revenue and a project payback period of less than two years.

> Note: Weighted average based on 1–5 year contracts

## Requirement: Price increase, expansion of customer segments

1. In Q3, the annual contract value per megawatt exceeded $25 million, while Q2 contracts ranged from $20 million to $25 million; the contracted price per GPU-hour rose by more than 20% on average in Q3 compared with Q2.
2. We have launched a new market-based pricing tool: reserve auction winning prices exceed the floor price by more than 15%; real-time spot computing power prices sometimes surpass on-demand pricing; and short-term cluster pricing for 3–6 months is more than twice the reserved computing power price.
3. We continue to develop emerging markets. Since its launch in the first quarter of 2026, the Asia-Pacific region has secured multiple customer contracts in Japan, South Korea, India, Australia, and Singapore; we have appointed country heads for South Korea and Japan to lead local market expansion.

## Diversified Procurement Model

* Short-term contracts (premium pricing model): reserve auctions, preemptible spot instances, pay-as-you-go billing, and premium short-term clusters. Both winning bidders in the reserve auction were new Nebius customers, with one of them subsequently increasing its contract size tenfold.
* Core model (1–3 year contracts): A large number of customers upgrade from preemptible compute to reserved compute, iterate to the next-generation GPU, and migrate from Token Factory to dedicated infrastructure.
* Long-term contracts (five-year term): All stem from capacity expansions by existing customers, who are procuring additional computing power; optimizing the contract tenor structure supports financial planning. In Q4, the early-stage AI cloud contract value has already reached the multi-billion-dollar level, with only a few months having passed since the first billion-dollar contract.

## Customer Onboarding Status: Cross-Industry, Multi-Channel Expansion

Leading enterprise data and AI platforms sign multi-year agreements for the first time

* Databricks: After rigorous evaluation, we selected Nebius AI Cloud, confirming its ability to support demanding AI research and development workloads.
* Datadog: By choosing Nebius to deploy its AI cloud, Datadog recognizes our AI-specific infrastructure, deep technical collaboration, and responsive technical support, resulting in an infrastructure partnership.
* Palantir: Designates Nebius as its preferred AI cloud partner, enabling Palantir customers to leverage Nebius infrastructure for fine-tuning and inference of sovereign AI models.
* Snowflake: Through partnership agreements, Snowflake's operations run on Nebius AI Cloud, demonstrating our ongoing expansion into top-tier technology enterprise customer segments.

Meanwhile, numerous cutting-edge native AI companies are joining at the same time:

* Cognition (the team behind Devin, an autonomous AI software engineer): Leverages Nebius's NVIDIA Vera Rubin large-scale cluster to meet computational demands, accelerate product iteration, and serve enterprise customers.
* Ortet (Medical Frontier Lab): Deploys the Blackwell cluster and will subsequently be given priority access to Vera Rubin computing resources, enabling expansion of its computational capacity.
* Cursive: a London-based AI lab founded by former DeepMind researchers, described Nebius as an "ideal computing partner."
* Distil Labs (Berlin post-training platform): Leveraging Nebius AI Cloud, it builds specialized models for AI agents using synthetic data.

## Ecosystem Partner Development

We have built an open ecosystem around Nebius, with partner offerings that address our customers' core needs:

1. Light-asset model partners: Leverage external capital and facilities to deliver computing power based on the Nebius architecture and cloud platform, expanding global supply of value-added AI computing resources.
2. Channel market partners: TD SYNNEX, Palantir, CDW, etc., leveraging a light-asset cooperation model to reach and serve more customers.
3. Full-stack technology partner: In collaboration with NVIDIA, Hugging Face, Reflection, OpenHands, and LangChain, our tools span models, agent frameworks, observability, and post-training, supporting the entire AI development lifecycle and backed by a developer support program.

## Expansion of customers' businesses within the platform

The inference service Token Factory has been live for less than a year yet is already approaching hundreds of millions of dollars in annualized revenue; many customers run multiple workloads simultaneously on the Nebius platform. Most initially came solely for compute power, but ultimately expanded their partnerships as they leveraged the platform's full suite of offerings.

We have integrated our proprietary infrastructure with hosting services into a vertically integrated platform, generating higher revenue per megawatt than pure infrastructure providers, and serving customers across diverse workloads, multiple GPU generations, and various contract structures.

* Applied Compute & Cursive: Leveraging Token Factory to extend model workflows from post-training on the platform to inference, providing scalable solutions for enterprise models and enhancing customer engagement across the entire AI lifecycle.
* Hark: Leveraging Token Factory to deliver low-latency inference for Hark Pro AI agents, continuously expanding use cases; several leading personal AI agent companies have adopted similar solutions.
* Prosus: Token Factory runs open-source models at scale to support its global e-commerce and local services businesses, which together serve one billion users.

Agent Infrastructure (Tavily): Over 3 million developers have built on Tavily, processing 350 million AI agent search requests each month.

* [monday.com](https://monday.com): AI products use Tavily's real-time web search to conduct corporate research, complete contact information, and monitor news.
* Bell Cyber: Automated threat analysis in the Security Operations Center processes 100,000 alerts per month, reducing the time to investigate each alert from 30 minutes to under 5 minutes, without requiring additional analysts.
* Ocean AI: The email security agent uses Tavily to verify senders and detect identity spoofing, completing one billion verifications per month and reducing investigation time from minutes to seconds.
* IBM Research: Selected Tavily to complete the post-training of the open-source Granite model family, with a second expansion of the collaboration scope in Q3.

## Computing Power Infrastructure: Focus Shifts to Proprietary Sites, with Capacity Steadily Scaling Up

### Progress on Computing Power Deployment

1. Q3 achieved the largest quarter-over-quarter increase in effective computing power in its history.
2. A total of four brand-new sites in the United States and Europe have commenced operations and begun generating revenue; at the New Jersey site, multiple batches of computing power were delivered continuously from Q3 through November.
3. Q4: Continuously launching new computing power; phased deployment and expansion of hosted data centers in the United States, Europe, and Israel.

### Next-generation chip
